questions.q: A partition wall has two layers of different materials $A$ and $B$ in contact with each other. They have the same thickness but the thermal conductivity of layer $A$ is twice that of $B$. At steady state, if the temperature difference across the layer $B$ is $50K$, then the corresponding temperature difference across the layer $A$ is
questions.solution:
Let $T$ be the junction temperature

Here, ${K}_{A} = 2{K}_{B}, T - {T}_{B} = 50K$

At the steady state ${H}_{A} = {H}_{B}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{K}_{A} A\left({T}_{A} - T\right)}{\dfrac{L}{2}} = \dfrac{{K}_{B} A\left(T - {T}_{B}\right)}{\dfrac{L}{2}}$

$⇒ 2{K}_{B} \left({T}_{A} -T\right) = {K}_{B} \left(T - {T}_{B}\right)$

$⇒ {T}_{A} - T = \dfrac{T - {T}_{B}}{2} = \dfrac{50}{2} =25K$

Rate of emission of energy $= \sigma T^{4} \text{S}$

Let m1 be the mass of sphere, C is specific heat and ~$\left(\text{d} \theta / \text{dt}\right)$,~the rate of cooling.

For sphere

$\sigma T^{4} \text{S} = {m}_{1} \text{C} {\left(\dfrac{\text{d} \theta}{\text{dt}}\right)}_{S}$ ...(i)

Let m2 be the mass of cube, C its specific heat and $\left(\text{d} \theta / \text{dt}\right)$,~the rate of cooling

$= \sqrt{\dfrac{2 \pi}{1 2}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{\pi}{6}}$

According to given problem mice = msteam, i.e.,

questions.q: Two uniform solid spheres made of copper have radii $15cm$ and $20cm$ respectively. Both of them are heated to a temperature of $70 ° C$ and then placed in a region of ambient temperature equal to $45 ° C$. What will be the ratio of the initial rates of cooling of both the spheres?
questions.solution:
For two bodies made up of same material, rate of loss of heat will depend only on their surface area for same temperature change.

$∴ \dfrac{{\left(\dfrac{dQ}{dt}\right)}_{1}}{{\left(\dfrac{dQ}{dt}\right)}_{2}} = \dfrac{{A}_{1}}{{A}_{2}} = {r}_{1}^{2}{r}_{2}^{2} \ldots \ldots \left(i\right)$

Ratio of initial rates of cooling$= \dfrac{{\left(\dfrac{d\theta}{dt}\right)}_{1}}{{\left(\dfrac{d\theta}{dt}\right)}_{2}}$

As, $\dfrac{dQ}{dt} = mc\dfrac{d\theta}{dt}$

$∴ \dfrac{{m}_{1}{c}_{1} ( d\theta / dt{)}_{1}}{{m}_{2}{c}_{2} ( d\theta / dt{)}_{2}} = {r}_{1}^{2}{r}_{2}^{2}$ ...[from (i)]

since, both the spheres are made up of copper,

${c}_{1} = {c}_{2} = c$.

$∴ \dfrac{{\left(\dfrac{d\theta}{dt}\right)}_{1}}{{\left(\dfrac{d\theta}{dt}\right)}_{2}} = \dfrac{{r}_{1}^{2} \times {m}_{2}}{{r}_{2}^{2} \times {m}_{1}}$

As, spheres have same densities,

$\dfrac{{m}_{1}}{{m}_{2}} = \dfrac{{V}_{1}}{{V}_{2}} = {r}_{1}^{3}{r}_{2}^{3}$

$∴ \dfrac{( d\theta / dt{)}_{1}}{( d\theta / dt{)}_{2}} = {r}_{1}^{2}{r}_{2}^{2} \times {r}_{2}^{3}{r}_{1}^{3} = \dfrac{{r}_{2}}{{r}_{1}} = \dfrac{20}{15} = \dfrac{4}{3} = 1 . 33$

Now as in this bridge [(P/Q) = (R/S)], so the bridge is balanced, i.e., the temperature at junctions C and D is equal and the rod CD becomes ineffective as no heat will flow through it.

Now as the thermal resistance of the bridge between junctions B and E is

$\dfrac{1}{{\text{R}}_{\text{BE}}} = \dfrac{1}{\left(\text{R} + \text{R}\right)} + \dfrac{1}{\left(\text{2R} + \text{2R}\right)} \text{,} \text{i.e.,} {\text{R}}_{\text{BE}} = \dfrac{4}{3} \text{R}$

The total resistance of bridge between A and E will be

      Req = RAB + RBE = 2R + (4/3) R = (10/3) R

So the net rate of flow of heat through the bridge will be

$\dfrac{\text{dQ}}{\text{dt}} = \dfrac{\text{\Delta} \text{\theta}}{{\text{R}}_{\text{eq}}} = \dfrac{\left(\text{60} - \text{10}\right)}{\left(\text{10/3}\right) \text{R}} = \dfrac{\text{15}}{\text{R}}$

$\text{But} [ \dfrac{\text{dQ}}{\text{dt}} {]}_{\text{AB}} = \dfrac{\text{dQ}}{\text{dt}} \text{,} \text{i.e.,} \dfrac{\text{60} - {\text{T}}_{\text{B}}}{2 \text{R}} = \dfrac{\text{15}}{\text{R}} \text{,} \text{i.e.,} {\text{T}}_{\text{B}} = {\text{30}}^{\text{o}} \text{C}$

Also at B

$[ \dfrac{\text{dQ}}{\text{dt}} {]}_{\text{AB}} = [ \dfrac{\text{dQ}}{\text{dt}} {]}_{\text{BC}} + [ \dfrac{\text{dQ}}{\text{dt}} {]}_{\text{BD}}$

and as     TC = TD = T,    30 = 3 (30 - T),

questions.q: A liquid having a coefficient of volume expansion $\gamma$ is filled in a cylindrical vessel made out of glass having coefficient of linear expansion $\alpha = \dfrac{\gamma}{5}$. At room temperature, the level of liquid in the vessel is ${l}_{0}$ and when the temperature is increased by $∆ T$, the level of liquid in the vessel becomes $l \approx {l}_{0}\left(1 + n\alpha ∆ T\right)$. What is the value of $n$? [Given, $\alpha ∆ T ≪ 1$]
questions.solution:
Let us assume that the volume of the liquid in the vessel is ${V}_{0}$ and the area of cross-section of the vessel is ${A}_{0}$, then

${l}_{0} = \dfrac{{V}_{0}}{{A}_{0}}$

Similarly,

$l = \dfrac{V}{A} = \dfrac{{V}_{0}\left(1 + \gamma ∆ T\right)}{{A}_{0}\left(1 + 2\alpha ∆ T\right)}$

$⇒ l = {l}_{0}\left(1 + \gamma ∆ T\right){\left(1 + 2\alpha ∆ T\right)}^{- 1}$

Using binomial approximation, we get

$l = {l}_{0}\left(1 + \gamma ∆ T\right)\left(1 - 2\alpha ∆ T\right)$

$⇒ l = {l}_{0}\left[1 + \left(\gamma - 2\alpha\right) ∆ T - 2\alpha\gamma{\left(∆ T\right)}^{2}\right]$

Neglecting $2\alpha\gamma{\left(∆ T\right)}^{2}$, since it is insignificant as compared to $\left(\gamma - 2\alpha\right) ∆ T$, we get

$l \approx {l}_{0}\left[1 + \left(\gamma - 2\alpha\right) ∆ T\right] ⇒ l \approx {l}_{0}\left[1 + \left(5\alpha - 2\alpha\right) ∆ T\right] ⇒ l \approx {l}_{0}\left[1 + 3\alpha ∆ T\right]$

So, $n = 3$

Consider a concentric spherical shell of radius $r$ and thickness $dr$ as shown in diagram. The radial rate of flow of heat through this shell in steady state will be,



$\text{H} = \dfrac{\text{d}\text{Q}}{\text{d}\text{t}} = - \text{KA}\dfrac{\text{d}\text{\theta}}{\text{d}\text{r}}$

Now in steady state, as no heat is absorbed, the rate of loss of heat by conduction is equal to that of supply, i.e., $H = P$, and here

& ${θ}_{1} - {θ}_{2} = T$ and $\text{a} ≃ \text{b} = \text{R}$

So Equation (i) becomes,

& & $\text{P} = 4\piR^{2}\text{KT} \left(\text{b} - \text{a}\right)

i.e thickness of shell is \left(b - a\right) = \dfrac{4\piR^{2}\text{KT}}{P}$

Density at temperature ${t}_{2}is, {d}_{2}$ = $\dfrac{{d}_{0}}{1 + \gamma{t}_{2}}

${f}_{1}V{d}_{1} = m = {f}_{2}V{d}_{2}$

questions.q: The rates of heat radiation from two patches of skin each of area $A$, on a patient's chest differ by $2 %$. If the patch of the lower temperature is at $300K$ and emissivity of both the patches is assumed to be unity, then what is the approximate temperature (in $K$) of the other patch? [Ignore all the higher-order terms in approximation]
questions.solution:
According to Stefan's law.

${E}_{1} = \sigma{T}^{4}and{E}_{2} = \sigma{\left(T + ∆ T\right)}^{4}$

$∴ \dfrac{{E}_{2} - {E}_{1}}{{E}_{1}} = \dfrac{\sigma{[ \left(T + ∆ T\right)}^{4} - {T}^{4} ]}{\sigma{T}^{4}} = 4\dfrac{∆ T}{T}$

Now, $\dfrac{{E}_{2} - {E}_{1}}{{E}_{1}} = \dfrac{2}{100} = 4\dfrac{∆ T}{300}$

$∴ ∆ T = \dfrac{300 \times 2}{4 \times 100} = 1.5K$

$∴$ Temperature of other patch = $T + ∆ T$

= 300 +1.5 = 301.5 K

questions.solution:
Given, ${K}_{c} = 400W{m}^{- 1}{K}^{- 1},$

${K}_{w} = 0.4W{m}^{- 1}{K}^{- 1}$

${\theta}_{1} = 100 ° C, {\theta}_{2} = 0 ° C$



In steady-state, the flow of heat will be the same throughout the whole system

$\dfrac{{K}_{w}A\left(100 - \theta\right)}{{10}^{- 3}} = \dfrac{{K}_{c}A\left(\theta - \theta′\right)}{\left(\dfrac{50}{100}\right)}$

Or $\left(100 - \theta\right) = \dfrac{{K}_{c}}{{K}_{w}} \times {10}^{- 3} \times \dfrac{\left(\theta - {\theta}^{′}\right)}{0.5}$

$= \dfrac{400}{0.4} \times {10}^{- 3} \times \dfrac{\left(\theta - \theta′\right)}{0.5}$

$\left(100 - \theta\right) = 2\left(\theta - \theta′\right)$

$\dfrac{( 100 - \theta ) {K}_{w} A}{{10}^{- 3}} = \dfrac{( {\theta}^{′} - 0 ) {K}_{w} A}{{10}^{- 3}}$

$100 - \theta = {\theta}^{′}$

Or $\left(100 - \theta\right) = 4\theta - 200$

$⇒ 5\theta = 300 ⇒ \theta = 60 ° C$

$∴ {\theta}^{′} = 100 - \theta = 100 - 60 = 40 ° C$

Hence, the temperature gradient along the bar

$= \dfrac{\theta - \theta′}{0.5} = \dfrac{60 - 40}{0.5} = 40 ° C{m}^{- 1}$

questions.q: $5g$ of water at $30 ° C$ and $5g$ of ice at $- 20 ° C$ are mixed together in a calorimeter. Find the final temperature of the mixture. Assume water equivalent of calorimeter to be negligible, specific heats of ice and water are $0. 5$ and $1calg^{- 1} ° C^{- 1}$, and latent heat of ice is $80calg^{- 1}$.
options:
$0 ° C$
&

$10 ° C$
&

$> 10 ° C$
&
questions.solution:
Here ice will absorb heat while hot water will release it.
So if $T$ is the final temperature of the mixture, heat given by water

${Q}_{1} = mc \Delta T = 5 \times 1 \times \left(30 - T\right)$

And heat absorbed by the ice

${Q}_{2} = 5 \times \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\left[0 - \left(- 20\right)\right] + 5 \times 80 + 5 \times 1\left(T - 0\right)$

So, by the principle of calorimetry ${Q}_{1} = {Q}_{2},$ i.e.,

$150 - 5T = 450 + 5T$

$T = - 30 ° C$

Which is impossible as a body cannot be cooled to a temperature below the temperature of the cooling body. The physical reason for this discrepancy is the heat remaining after changing the temperature of ice from -20 to 0^{o}C with some ice left unmelted and we are taking it for granted that heat is transferred from water at 0^{o}C to ice at 0^{o}C so that temperature below 0^{o}C.
However, as heat cannot flow from one body (water) to the other (ice) at the same temperature (0^{o}C), the temperature of the system will not fall below 0^{o}C.

From Stefan's law, the rate at which energy is radiated by sun at its surface is& $P = \sigma \times 4\piR^{2}T^{4}$

$= \pi{r}_{0}^{2} \times I$

If the fractional length of aluminium is $\dfrac{p}{q}$ where $p and q$ are the least positive integers, then what is the value of $\left(p + q\right)$? (linear coefficients of thermal expansion of aluminium and steel are $23 \times {10}^{- 6} ° {C}^{- 1} and 12 \times {10}^{- 6} ° {C}^{- 1}$, respectively)
questions.solution:
The change in length of wire $= {l ⁡}_{\text{A} l ⁡} {\alpha}_{\text{A} l ⁡} \Delta \theta + {l ⁡}_{\text{st}} {\alpha}_{\text{st}} \Delta \theta$ associated with a temperature change of $\Delta \theta$, where ${\alpha}_{\text{A} l ⁡}$ and ${\alpha}_{\text{St}}$ are the coefficient of linear expansion of aluminium and steel, respectively

${\alpha}_{\text{A}l ⁡} = 23 \times 1{0}^{- 6}{}^{∘}{\text{C}}^{- 1}$

${\alpha}_{\text{St}} = 12 \times 1{0}^{- 6}{}^{∘}{\text{C}}^{- 1}$

The effective coefficient of linear expansion of the two segments of wire $= 1 9 \times 1 {0}^{- 6} / {}^{∘} \text{C}$

${l ⁡}_{1} {\alpha}_{\text{A} l ⁡} \Delta \theta + {l ⁡}_{2} {\alpha}_{\text{St}} \Delta \theta = \left({l ⁡}_{1} + {l ⁡}_{2}\right) \alpha \Delta \theta$

$\dfrac{{l ⁡}_{1}}{\left({l ⁡}_{1} + {l ⁡}_{2}\right)} = \dfrac{\alpha - \dfrac{{l ⁡}_{2}}{\left({l ⁡}_{1} + {l ⁡}_{2}\right)} {\alpha}_{\text{st}}}{{\alpha}_{\text{A} l ⁡}}$

$\left[\dfrac{{l ⁡}_{1}}{{l ⁡}_{1} + {l ⁡}_{2}} = \text{x} {l ⁡}_{1} + {l ⁡}_{2} = l ⁡ \left(\dfrac{{l ⁡}_{2}}{{l ⁡}_{1} + {l ⁡}_{2}}\right) = 1 - \text{x}\right]$

$\text{x} = \dfrac{\alpha - \left(1 - \text{x}\right) {\alpha}_{\text{st}}}{{\alpha}_{\text{A} l ⁡}}$

$\text{x} = \dfrac{\alpha - {\alpha}_{\text{st}}}{{\alpha}_{\text{A}l ⁡} - {\alpha}_{\text{st}}} = \dfrac{19 \times 1{0}^{- 6} - 12 \times 1{0}^{- 6}}{23 \times 1{0}^{- 6} - 12 \times 1{0}^{- 6}} = \dfrac{7}{11} = \dfrac{p}{q}$

So, $p + q = 18$

questions.q: Calculate the compressional force required to prevent the metallic rod of length $l cm$ and cross-sectional area $A{cm}^{2}$when heated through $t ° C$, from expanding lengthwise. questions.solution:
The change in natural length $= \Delta {l ⁡}_{t} = l ⁡ \alpha \text{t}$
The natural length of rod at temperature $t^{∘} \text{C} = l ⁡ + l ⁡ \alpha \text{t}$
The decrease in natural length due to developed stress $= \Delta l ⁡$
But the length of rod remains constant.

$∴ \Delta {l ⁡}_{t} - \Delta l ⁡ = 0$

$∴ \Delta l ⁡ = \Delta {l ⁡}_{t} = l ⁡ \alpha \text{t}$

$∴ \text{E} = \dfrac{\text{stress}}{\text{strain}} = \dfrac{\text{F/A}}{\dfrac{- \Delta l ⁡}{l ⁡ + \Delta {l ⁡}_{t}}}$

$∴ \text{E} = - \dfrac{\text{EA} \Delta l ⁡}{l ⁡ + \Delta {l ⁡}_{t}} = - \dfrac{\text{EA} \Delta {l ⁡}_{t}}{l ⁡ + \Delta {l ⁡}_{t}}$

$= - \dfrac{\text{EA} l ⁡ \alpha \text{t}}{l ⁡ + l ⁡ \alpha \text{t}} = - \dfrac{\text{EA} \alpha \text{t}}{\left(1 + \alpha \text{t}\right)}$
